acceptance: Capability model is deny-by-default with the canon hierarchy (filesystem.read/write/roots, network.http/tcp/udp, process.spawn, env.read, clock.wall, clock.monotonic, crypto.random, crypto.keystore, poppy.*); granting an ancestor implies its descendants, and a host or project policy may only narrow a grant, never widen it silently

AHS is consumed as data: modules, types, host values, handles, functions, params, return contracts, mutability, async, docs, capabilities and deprecation/version are described by the host, so the compiler reaches a host surface without knowing which host it is
Host values copy by value and external identity belongs to the host: no Rust reference, lifetime or engine type crosses the script boundary
Generational handles never use freed state: a stale or foreign-generation access resolves to none or a Failure according to the declared contract, never a Rust panic and never a use-after-free
A missing capability is a runtime fault with the stable code AIPO_RT_CAPABILITY_DENIED carrying its target/capability context, instead of a silently absent or faked API
A binding created inside a scoped host callback cannot escape it, enforced at the VM heap-publication points (SetGlobal, Return, SetField, SetIndex, BuildList, BuildDict)
Nondeterministic sources (time.now, time.monotonic) are reached only through the capability layer and can be replaced by a deterministic test profile
cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo test --workspace --all-targets and cargo doc --workspace --no-deps are all green

objective: Prove the host-neutral ABI defined by Wave 4: consume an AHS (host surface description as data), a deny-by-default capability model, host values that copy by value with host-owned external identity, and generational handles that never use-after-free (stale access yields none or a Failure per contract). General abstractions only: bytecode and IR must never know about a specific engine, and the VM reaches host services solely through the capability layer.
title: Host ABI: capability model, host values and generational handles
